title: Q226 imaging simulation: tissue classes (CT HU, MRI T1/T2/PD at 1.5 T), structure -> class mapping rules, bone model, windows, MR sequence presets
licence: PRIVATE clinical layer (clinical/LICENSE_PRIVATE.md). Numbers are literature-based model inputs, not measurements of the two bodies.
honesty: This table drives a SIMULATION computed from segmented anatomical meshes. It is not a scan and it contains no patient data.

Every row carries a status. 'verified_abstract': the number is stated (or is a direct evaluation of a formula stated) in a PubMed abstract read on 2026-10-12. 'secondary_checked': the number was found in a secondary source that cites the primary paper; the primary table was not read. 'recalled_unverified': the citation exists in PubMed (PMID checked) but the numeric value comes from the author's recollection of the paper / textbook range and was NOT re-read -- treat as UNVERIFIED. 'assumption': a modelling choice with no single source.

MRI numbers are for 1.5 T. 3 T values from the literature are shortened to 1.5 T only where the row says 'derived'. A single T1/T2 per class hides multi-exponential decay, magnetisation transfer, orientation (magic-angle) effects, B1/B0 inhomogeneity, chemical-shift and susceptibility artefacts, and motion; none of these are simulated.
Flow (void / inflow) and the post-gadolinium T1 values are schematic.

bottomley1984.cite: Bottomley PA, Foster TH, Argersinger RE, Pfeifer LM. A review of normal tissue hydrogen NMR relaxation times and relaxation mechanisms from 1-100 MHz. Med Phys 1984;11:425-448
bottomley1984.used_for: frequency dependence of T1, T2 independent of field; tissue-type ordering

gold2004.cite: Gold GE, Han E, Stainsby J, Wright G, Brittain J, Beaulieu C. Musculoskeletal MRI at 3.0 T: relaxation times and image contrast. AJR 2004;183:343-351
gold2004.used_for: cartilage, muscle, synovial fluid, marrow, subcutaneous fat at 1.5 and 3 T (numbers NOT in the abstract)

debazelaire2004.cite: de Bazelaire CMJ, Duhamel GD, Rofsky NM, Alsop DC. MR imaging relaxation times of abdominal and pelvic tissues measured in vivo at 3.0 T. Radiology 2004;230:652-659
debazelaire2004.used_for: 3 T abdominal values in the abstract (kidney cortex 1142/76, medulla 1545/81, liver 809/34, spleen 1328/61, pancreas 725/43, paravertebral muscle 898/29, L4 marrow 586/49, subcutaneous fat 382/68 ms; prostate, myometrium); T1 on average 21% longer at 3 T than 1.5 T for kidney cortex, liver, spleen

stanisz2005.cite: Stanisz GJ, Odrobina EE, Pun J, Escaravage M, Graham SJ, Bronskill MJ, Henkelman RM. T1, T2 relaxation and magnetization transfer in tissue at 3T. Magn Reson Med 2005;54:507-512
stanisz2005.used_for: T2 field-independence statement (abstract); tissue tables not read

rooney2007.cite: Rooney WD, Johnson G, Li X, Cohen ER, Kim SG, Ugurbil K, Springer CS. Magnetic field and tissue dependencies of human brain longitudinal 1H2O relaxation in vivo. Magn Reson Med 2007;57:308-318
rooney2007.used_for: abstract: T1(s) = 0.583 B0^0.382 (white matter), 0.857 B0^0.376 (internal gray matter), 1.35 B0^0.340 (blood), CSF 4.3 s independent of field -> evaluated at 1.5 T

wansapura1999.cite: Wansapura JP, Holland SK, Dunn RS, Ball WS. NMR relaxation times in the human brain at 3.0 tesla. J Magn Reson Imaging 1999;9:531-538
wansapura1999.used_for: 3 T brain T1 (gray 1331, white 832 ms, abstract); the T2 numbers in the abstract are internally inconsistent and are not used

schneider2000.cite: Schneider W, Bortfeld T, Schlegel W. Correlation between CT numbers and tissue parameters needed for Monte Carlo simulations of clinical dose distributions. Phys Med Biol 2000;45:459-478
schneider2000.used_for: CT numbers calculated for 71 tissues from ICRU/ICRP composition (numbers NOT in the abstract)

lamba2014.cite: Lamba R, McGahan JP, Corwin MT, Li CS, Tran T, Seibert JA, Boone JM. CT Hounsfield numbers of soft tissues on unenhanced abdominal CT scans: variability between two different manufacturers' MDCT scanners. AJR 2014;203:1013-1020
lamba2014.used_for: full text read: HU scale fixed points (water 0, air -1000); liver/spleen/renal cortex/psoas/subcutaneous-fat sites vary by scanner (differences up to 10.5 HU); hepatic steatosis threshold 40 HU; per-site mean tables are images not in the retrieved text

schreiber2011.cite: Schreiber JJ, Anderson PA, Rosas HG, Buchholz AL, Au AG. Hounsfield units for assessing bone mineral density and strength: a tool for osteoporosis management. J Bone Joint Surg Am 2011;93:1057-1063
schreiber2011.used_for: vertebral cancellous HU scale (numbers NOT in the abstract)

pickhardt2013.cite: Pickhardt PJ, Pooler BD, Lauder T, del Rio AM, Bruce RJ, Binkley N. Opportunistic screening for osteoporosis using abdominal computed tomography scans obtained for other indications. Ann Intern Med 2013;158:588-595
pickhardt2013.used_for: abstract: L1 trabecular attenuation thresholds 110 / 145 / 160 / 200 HU (osteoporotic vs normal)

woodard1986.cite: Woodard HQ, White DR. The composition of body tissues. Br J Radiol 1986;59:1209-1218
woodard1986.used_for: water / lipid / protein / ash fractions and densities of 56 tissues -> relative proton density (numbers NOT in the abstract)

hounsfield1973.cite: Hounsfield GN. Computerized transverse axial scanning (tomography): Part 1. Description of system. Br J Radiol 1973;46:1016-1022
hounsfield1973.used_for: definition of the CT number scale

icru44.cite: ICRU Report 44. Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement. International Commission on Radiation Units and Measurements, 1989
icru44.used_for: reference tissue composition and density behind the HU ranges (book, not in PubMed, not re-read)

textbook_mr.cite: Standard MR physics: spin-echo S = PD (1 - exp(-TR/T1)) exp(-TE/T2); inversion recovery S = PD |1 - 2 exp(-TI/T1) + exp(-TR/T1)| exp(-TE/T2); spoiled gradient echo S = PD sin(a)(1 - E1)/(1 - E1 cos a) exp(-TE/T2*), E1 = exp(-TR/T1) (e.g. Bernstein, Handbook of MRI Pulse Sequences, 2004)

textbook_ct.cite: Textbook CT-number ranges (e.g. Bushberg, The Essential Physics of Medical Imaging; Brant & Helms, Fundamentals of Diagnostic Radiology)
textbook_ct.used_for: HU ranges of lung, fat, water, CSF, blood, muscle, organs, cancellous and cortical bone; not re-read

bone_model.note: The meshes are outer surfaces only. Cortex vs medullary / cancellous interior is MODELLED from the slice itself: pixels within a cortical thickness of the bone edge = cortical bone; inside, long-bone shaft (central part of the PCA axis) = medullary canal (yellow marrow), otherwise cancellous bone. Thicknesses are assumptions (femoral mid-shaft cortex ~ 5-7 mm of a ~28 mm outer diameter is the anchor), NOT measured on these bodies.

flat_irregular.label: vertebra / pelvis / scapula / rib / carpal / tarsal ...

bone_model.skin_note: the thin skin rim is drawn at the body boundary of the slice (assumption: dermis + epidermis ~ 1.5-2 mm on the trunk)

baseline.note: Space inside the skin that no structure covers = subcutaneous / intermuscular fat and loose connective tissue (a documented ASSUMPTION: the segmentations do not contain every fascial plane and fat pad). Outside the skin = air. Where the model has no skin (arms or feet cut by the field of view) the slice shows air there.

mapping_rules.note: First matching rule wins. Input = viewer category (cat), structure id and name (lower case, underscores -> spaces), vt ('v' = Z-Anatomy vein flag). Regexes use only the JS/Python common subset so the report script and the add-on agree (a test compares them).

rules.why: all other bones: thin cortex + cancellous interior
ligaments, capsules, retinacula, tendons, fascia = dense fibrous tissue
bursae and tendon sheaths = synovial fluid
central white-matter tracts filed under nerve
central gray structures filed under nerve (Z-Anatomy)
spinal cord (names with 'white matter' are caught next)
gyri, sulci, lobes, nuclei = gray matter
other solid organs, ducts, glands and pelvic organs

fallback.why: no rule matched: generic soft tissue, listed in the mapping report
